video players for local media in the DeepSeek Harness chat, plus xAI Grok Imagine video generation.
# dsh-plugin-media-gen

Audio and video playback inside the DeepSeek Harness
chat, plus xAI Grok Imagine video generation.

The harness already renders images that point at local files; it has no equivalent
for video or audi
o. This plugin fills that gap from the plugin layer:

- **`show_media`** — display any existing local image, video or audio file.
- **`generate_video`** —
generate a clip with xAI Grok Imagine and show it.

Both render into a **Turn-level card** under the assistant's prose, and also into a
keyed tool row,

so the player is visible without expanding the collapsible tool
group.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then, in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`, add the `link:` dependency and
`dsh-plugin-media-ge
n` to `dsh.profile.bundles`. Restart the app.
## Tools
### `show_media`
| Parameter | Type | Notes |

| `path` | string | **Required.** Absolute path to the file. |
| `title` | string | Optional caption
above the player. |

Accepted extensions — image: `png jpg jpeg webp gif avif bmp`; video: `mp4 mov m4v
webm mkv`; audio:

`mp3 wav m4a flac ogg opus aac`. Anything else is refused with a
message that lists the supported s

et. Returns `{ path, kind, bytes }` and records
`{ path, title? }` in `presentationMeta`, which is w

here the card reads the path
from (no prose parsing).
### `generate_video`

Calls xAI's Imagine API (`POST /v1/videos/generations`, poll
`GET /v1/videos/{id}`), downloads the M

P4 into `<DSH_HOME>/media/`, and returns its
absolute path. Parameters: `prompt` (required), `image_

path`, `duration` (1–15 s),
`aspect_ratio`, `resolution`, `model`, `generate_audio`, `output_dir`.

The API key is resolved per call from `GROK_API_KEY`, either from the launch
environment or from `~/
.dsh/.credentials.yaml`, so rotating it needs no restart.
## Why a custom media route

The harness route `GET /api/file` serves local files, but it ignores the `Range`
header and answers

every request with a full `200` body. A `<video>` asks for byte
ranges, receives a full-body `200`,

and fires `error`; audio survives because its
pipeline tolerates a full response. This plugin theref

ore registers its own
authenticated route:
`GET|HEAD /api/media-gen/file?path=<absolute>`

- `200` with `Accept-Ranges: bytes` and the exact MIME type
- `206` with `Content-Range` for `bytes=

a-b`, `bytes=a-` and `bytes=-n`
- `416` with `Content-Range: bytes */<size>` for an unsatisfiable ra

nge
- streaming instead of buffering the file

The client tries this route first and falls back to `/api/file`, then to a plain
link, so the plugin
keeps working if the connection carrier is unavailable.
## Two surfaces, one card

Tool calls collapse into a foldable group, so a card registered only in
`tool.call.toolview` is hidd

en until the group is expanded. The primary surface is
the **Turn tail**: a Turn Definition (`media-

shown`) accumulates the paths that
media tools produced, and the card registered in `conversation.ch

at.turnTail` draws
them under the closing prose — the same seat `present` and `schedule_create` use.

Media tool results quote the path (`Shown audio: "/…/file.mp3" (2.8 MB)`) so a file
name containing

spaces can still be extracted when the definition replays a
session.
## Limitations

- The player lives in the Turn card and the tool row. It never appears as a bare
assistant block and

never from Markdown, because the harness does not expose its
text renderer as an extension point.
-

`generate_video` blocks the turn while polling; generation takes one to three
minutes and the decla

red timeout is fifteen.
- Images still render through Markdown; `show_media` exists mainly for video

and
audio, where Markdown does not reach.
## Development notes

- No `@deepseek-ai/*` imports: a third-party plugin lives outside the app's bundled
`node_modules`,

so those specifiers do not resolve. Tool definitions are the
plain objects `defineTool` would have p

roduced.
- The browser half ships in the harness's `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` format and
require

s only `react`.
- Everything here can be exercised without spending credits: the tools against a
scr

ipted `fetch`, the media route against real files, and the card against a
simulated React.
